This integration shows a **TOLO steam generator or sauna with its App Box** in
Gladys, on the local network (UDP, port 51500), with no account and no
cloud. **Never tested with a real device.** Not affiliated with TOLO.

> **Safety.** A steam room or a sauna heats. Never start heating from afar
> without making sure nobody is inside. Turning on from Gladys is **off by
> default**; turning off is held back by no option and no command in
> progress (it may still fail if the App Box is unreachable).

## What you get

One device in the Discovery tab, with:

- **Heating on** (yes/no, read only) and the **status** as text ("Off",
  "Heating", "Keeping warm", "On, not heating");
- measured **temperature** and **humidity**, the **setpoint**;
- **time left** (minutes) on the timer;
- **water level** (0, 33, 66 or 100 %) and **tank temperature**;
- **lamp** (on/off) and **fan** (on/off);
- two buttons: **Turn on (heat)** and **Turn off**.

Heating has no switch: an "everything on" from Google Home, Alexa, HomeKit,
MCP or a scene cannot start it. It may turn the lamp or the fan on.

## Setup

1. Give the App Box a **fixed address** in your router (a fixed DHCP lease).
2. In Gladys, open the TOLO integration and enter that **IP address** (IPv4,
   for instance 192.168.1.50). Refused: a name, broadcast addresses
   (including any address ending in .255), multicast, loopback, 0.x.x.x and
   169.254.x.x.
3. Save, then add the device from the **Discovery** tab (it shows up after
   the first successful read).
4. To start heating from Gladys, turn on **Allow heating from Gladys**, and
   set the **session duration** (30 min by default, 1 to 60 min, the limit
   of the App Box) and the **highest setpoint** (50 °C by default, 35 to
   60 °C, the range of the App Box).

The App Box is read every 30 s (10 s to 1 h). The periodic reads are never
closer than the interval, even after a restart of the integration, a reconnection to Gladys, the "Test the
connection" button or a Discovery scan. A command adds its own reads (fresh
read, read back), then two follow-up reads 5 s and 20 s later.

The protocol gives no serial number nor MAC address: the device is "the App
Box answering at the configured address". Changing the address keeps the
same device in Gladys.

## The commands

### Turn off

Any value received presses it (0, 1, true…). Turning off is held back
neither by the heating option, nor by a command in progress, nor by a read
in progress, nor by an App Box that stopped answering. Right after a
restart, before the configuration is read again, it goes to the address
cached by Gladys (or the one of a guard kept in `/data`). It is sent with no
read before it (never "already off"): **4 datagrams at most**, 400 ms apart,
while the App Box stays silent or a network error (closed port, unreachable
host) ends an attempt; each attempt goes from a fresh socket. It cancels a
turn on that has not left yet; if a turn on had already left, it is sent
again when that turn on settles.

It is confirmed only by a read showing the App Box off (also after an answer
saying "refused": the state read is what counts). Possible answers:

- success: read off;
- "Sent, without confirmation": no answer, no read back, or read still on;
- "The App Box answered with a refusal, but reads: …": refused and read
  still on;
- "Not sent": no datagram could leave;
- "No App Box address configured": no address known.

Without confirmation, a guard of 2 minutes is set (kept in `/data`, it
survives a restart: a read then goes 5 s after the start, whatever the
interval). During the guard, a periodic or follow-up read that sees the App
Box on sends the turn off again (3 times at most); the read back of a
command, and reads made while a turn off or a turn on is in flight, send
nothing. It may also turn off heating started from the App Box or the TOLO
app within those 2 minutes: on purpose. During the guard, a turn on from
Gladys is refused and only a lower setpoint is accepted.

### Turn on (heat)

It takes exactly 1. Refused, no power on sent, in these cases:

- a value other than 1, or no address configured;
- "Allow heating from Gladys" is off (checked on arrival, after the read,
  then right before every datagram);
- a turn off is in flight, not confirmed yet (its guard), or asked during
  the turn on;
- another turn on is in progress, or the previous one is not confirmed yet
  (2 minutes at most);
- the App Box does not answer the fresh read (status and settings) within
  1.5 s, or its power state is unreadable;
- the timer or the setpoint could not be set and read back (it may have
  been written: that heats nothing);
- the configuration (address) changed meanwhile;
- the power on cannot leave within 3.5 s of the click.

Steps: a fresh read of the status and the settings (never the state in
memory); already on: nothing sent; otherwise the **timer** of the App Box is
set to the session duration (never "no timer") and a setpoint above the
highest one is **lowered** to it, both read back; only then does the power
on leave. A read of less than 10 s showing the App Box already on is enough
to send nothing.

Answers after the power on (always followed by a read):

- success: read on, with a timer of 1 minute to the session duration;
- "Turned on, timer not confirmed": read on without that timer. The
  integration then writes the timer again in the background and reads; if
  it is still missing, it **turns the App Box off**, logs it and says it in
  the status;
- "Turned on, but a turn off was asked after it had left": the turn off is
  sent again;
- "The App Box answered with a refusal, but reads: …" or "The App Box
  refused the command": depending on the state read;
- "Sent, without confirmation": no answer, no read back, or read off.

**Timer (not checked on a real device).** According to tololib, the App Box
stops by itself at the end of its timer. A session started from Gladys is
held to its duration, also when the timer is changed or removed at the
panel; **the integration never extends a session itself**:

- every read of the session checks that a timer of 1 minute to what is
  left of the session runs (0 is accepted only in its last minute);
- otherwise the timer is written again with **what is left** of the
  session (1 min at least; planned end passed: turned off directly), then
  read strictly (1 minute to the value written); otherwise the App Box is
  turned off;
- a dedicated read goes at the planned end + 2 minutes: still on (or no
  read), the App Box is turned off, with a guard, a log line and a message
  in the status;
- this watch is kept in `/data`: after a restart it goes on and its end
  read is scheduled again.

A session started elsewhere (App Box, TOLO app) is not watched, except in
these windows.

Limit: the watch ends only on a read showing the App Box off. A session
started again at the panel (or from the TOLO app) before the integration
has read the end of the Gladys session (one read interval at most, and up
to 2 minutes after the planned end), or, after a restart of the
integration, within 10 minutes after the planned end, is taken for the
Gladys session: it may be turned off.

### Setpoint

Refused when the option is off, when the value is not a whole number from
35 °C to the highest setpoint (checked again right before the datagram),
when another setpoint is in progress, when the configuration changed
meanwhile, when it cannot leave within 3.5 s, or, while a turn off is in
flight or not confirmed, when it is not lower than the setpoint known.
According to tololib, changing the setpoint does not turn the App Box on;
the power state is read after it, and should the App Box have gone from off
to on (no turn on from Gladys in progress), it is turned off at once and the
setpoint refused. Confirmed by a read of the settings.

### Lamp and fan

Plain on/off (0 or 1), one command at a time each, confirmed by a read.
According to tololib, the lamp and the fan only drive their output (not
checked on a real App Box); should a lamp or fan command turn the App Box
on (off on a read of less than 10 s, made right before when needed, and on
right after), the integration turns it off at once and refuses the
command.

## Troubleshooting

- **The App Box does not answer**: the status says so, the device is shown
  unreachable, next try after 30 s, 1, 2 then 5 min (never faster than the
  interval). A turn off is still sent.
- Only answers from **the address and port of the App Box**, well formed
  (prefix, suffix, checksum, length) and of the command sent are taken;
  every exchange has its own socket, so a late answer of an earlier exchange
  is never taken for another one's.
- The container must reach the App Box in UDP (Docker bridge network:
  unicast traffic normally goes out to the local network).

## Limits

- **Protocol not documented** by TOLO: the integration follows the
  open-source tololib library, written by observing the App Box. A firmware
  may change it.
- No automatic discovery: the address is typed by hand.
- No humidity setpoint, aroma therapy, salt bath, sweep nor fan timer yet.
- One App Box per integration.

## Data

`/data/tolo-state.json` holds only the time of the last read and the guard
of a turn off in progress (App Box address, end time, number of resends),
and the watch of a session started from Gladys (App Box address, duration,
planned end). No secret exists in this integration.

Based on the tololib Python library (MIT, Matthias Lohr), ported to
JavaScript: see `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

## Konfigurationseinstellungen

Diese Einstellungen fragt TOLO in seinem Konfigurationsbildschirm in Gladys ab.

| Einstellung | Typ | Pflichtfeld | Beschreibung |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your TOLO App Box | `section` | Nein | Shows a TOLO steam generator or sauna with its App Box in Gladys, on the local network (UDP port 51500, no account, no cloud): status, temperature, humidity, setpoint, time left, water level, lamp, fan. Turning off is never held back by the heating option; heating from Gladys (turning on and the setpoint) is off until you allow it below. The App Box protocol is not published by TOLO: this integration follows the open-source tololib library. Give the App Box a fixed address in your router, enter it below, save, then add the device from the Discovery tab. A steam room or a sauna heats: never start it from afar without making sure nobody is inside. Never tested with a real device. Not affiliated with TOLO. |
| IP address of the App Box | `string` | Ja | An IPv4 address of your local network, such as 192.168.1.50 (shown in your router's list of devices). Give it a fixed lease: the protocol has no serial number, so Gladys trusts the App Box answering at this address. |
| Allow heating from Gladys | `boolean` | Nein | Off by default. On: the "Turn on (heat)" button and the setpoint may start or change heating; each turn on first sets the timer of the App Box to the session duration below. Off: they refuse every request. Turning off is never held back by this option. |
| Session duration (min) | `number` | Nein | The timer set on the App Box before every turn on from Gladys (30 min by default; 60 min, the limit of the App Box, at most; never "no timer"). According to tololib, the App Box should stop by itself after this time (not checked on a real device): a turn on is confirmed only when a read shows this timer running, and a session from Gladys found without it gets the timer again, then is turned off. |
| Highest setpoint (°C) | `number` | Nein | Gladys never asks for more (50 °C by default; 35 to 60 °C, the range of the App Box). A setpoint above it on the App Box is lowered to it before a turn on from Gladys. |
| Refresh interval (s) | `number` | Nein | How often the App Box is read, in seconds. The periodic reads are never closer than this interval, even after a restart; a command adds its own reads. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | Nein | Used for the feature names of the devices added from now on, for the status texts and for the command errors. |

## So installierst du TOLO in Gladys

1. Öffne in Gladys **Integrationen**: TOLO erscheint im Katalog neben den nativen Integrationen, mit einem Community-Badge.
2. Klicke auf **Installieren**. Gladys lädt das Docker-Image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-tolo:0.1.1`) herunter, startet es in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox und erzeugt die Oberfläche der Integration (Geräte, Erkennung und Konfiguration).
3. Öffne den Bildschirm **Konfiguration** der Integration, fülle die Einstellungen aus und speichere.
4. Du kannst sie auch direkt über die URL ihres Repositorys installieren: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-tolo](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-tolo).

TOLO benötigt Gladys `>=5.1.0`. Der Katalog in Gladys wird stündlich aktualisiert, eine neue Version ist also spätestens eine Stunde nach ihrer Veröffentlichung verfügbar.

Du nutzt Gladys noch nicht? Es ist kostenlos und Open Source: [folge der Installationsanleitung](/de/docs/), um loszulegen.

## Über externe Integrationen

TOLO ist eine **externe Integration**: eine Community-Integration, die als Docker-Container verpackt und auf GitHub veröffentlicht wird. Gladys installiert sie mit einem Klick und führt sie in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox aus. Sie wird von [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7) veröffentlicht und gepflegt, nicht vom Gladys-Kernteam.
